messages:
anna_support: heads up — customer XYZ hitting intermittent 502/504s from hosted inference edge since ~2026-03-17T16:23:00Z. They see timeouts and failed streaming chunks when sending large batched embedding requests. sample curl + trace id below. pinging eng/sre for triage.

customer_xyz: thanks, we started seeing ~30% of requests erroring after a spike of large batches. request id: trace=abc123-edge. latency jumps to 3-8s before failing.

mike_sre: can you paste the raw client request and any edge logs? also which region (eu1/us-east)?

anna_support: pasted curl; region eu1. curl sample: ```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["...big payload..."]}'
```
edge log snippet: ```
[16:23:12.451] upstream reset: RST_STREAM, code=0, downstream_id=512, route=eu1-ingress
[16:23:12.452] 502 while proxying to midfront (conn-window=exhausted) trace=abc123-edge
```

julia_eng: :eyes: reading logs — I see many long-lived streaming connections and h2 keepalive churn. looks like the midfront pool is hitting conn-window saturation when the client sends many concurrent large-batch requests. that aligns with streaming chunk timeouts.

mike_sre: can you repro locally with smaller scale? try this quick stress repro (from host with curl): ```
for i in {1..150}; do \
  curl -sS -X POST https://eu1.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @large_batch.json &
done; wait
```
should produce similar connwindow pressure in ~1-2m.

anna_support: customer confirmed they applied similar script for parallel uploads. also noticed errors correlate with a burst after a billing job that spiked metadata headers.

sam_prodops: suggestion — temporarily reduce allowed concurrent batch size at edge for hosted API to avoid pool exhaustion. we can add a quick nginx/ envoy rate-limit or conn-window guard until a permanent fix.

julia_eng: agree. root cause hypothesis: the edge/midfront routing uses a shared upstream with limited h2 stream window. large payloads + long stream times cause stream slots to be held, blocking new upstream streams and producing 502/504 on new requests. fix options: 1) increase upstream conn window / keepalive pool, 2) add smart per-tenant concurrency limiter (short-term), 3) encourage smaller batch sizes + client backoff.

anna_support: can we do a hotfix: increase midfront upstream max_concurrent_streams by 50% and add a temporary per-client conn cap? owner?

mike_sre: i can roll a canary config to eu1 midfront in 10m. i'll also enable extra metrics on h2_streams_in_use and conn_window_waits. deploybot: kick off canary eu1-midfront-config-2026-03-17-1

deploybot: started canary deployment eu1-midfront-config-2026-03-17-1 -> 5% hosts. status: in_progress.

customer_xyz: appreciate the quick follow-up. can you also share recommended client-side mitigation? our product can't immediately reduce batch size.

julia_eng: client-side workaround: add jittered backoff + chunking to split a single big batch into smaller sub-requests (e.g., <= 50 inputs). also switch to non-streaming short-lived requests if possible. we'll document recommended limits in the hosted API best-practices page.

sam_prodops: post-canary, if stable, we'll make a rolling config to 100% and add a short-lived rate-limit rule for requests with payload > 1MB. also add alerting on conn_window_wait_count > 5/min.

mike_sre: quick triage checklist created: - repro script (done) - enable h2 metrics (in progress) - canary config (started) - customer mitigation guidance (done) - postmortem if rollbacks needed. assigning owners: mike_sre (canary + metrics), julia_eng (fix/design), sam_prodops (temporary rate-limit), anna_support (customer comms).

anna_support: thanks team — I'll update customer and keep thread running. tagging @customer_xyz when canary is at 100% and we confirm reduction in 502s. :thumbsup:
